cf.title: Fix race with LLVM and bison.

input.subject: Fix race with LLVM and bison.

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a or 1b: the build failure is reported with a reproduction, and the fix copies the rule src/backend/common.mk already uses. The one surviving objection, maintenance-fit-1, is a fixable scope point at level 2. The remaining decision is the backpatch risk for out-of-tree extensions, which a committer who knows the make build system has to judge.

brief.title: Make pgxs .bc files depend on .o files to fix LLVM build race
brief.problem: With --with-llvm and parallel make, contrib/cube and contrib/seg can fail because bitcode for cubescan.c or segscan.c compiles before bison generates cubeparse.h or segparse.h. Zsolt Parragi reports that pg_plan_advice is affected too. The failure hits anyone building contrib or pgxs extensions with LLVM enabled.
brief.proposed_design: The patch makes each .bc file for MODULES in pgxs.mk depend on its .o file, as src/backend/common.mk already does for backend objects. The .o file already carries the dependencies on generated headers, so the .bc build waits for them. An earlier alternative added per-module rules only to the cube and seg Makefiles.
user_visible_surface: Changed make dependency rules in src/makefiles/pgxs.mk, which out-of-tree extensions use to build bitcode.
author_claims: Andres Freund says `make -C contrib/cube cubescan.bc` shows the problem without the sleep-based reproduction patch.
Andres Freund says the backend avoids the race because each .bc file already depends on the .o file.
Andres Freund fears that backpatching could break some extensions, so he leans toward fixing master only.
Zsolt Parragi says a generic fix in pgxs.mk covers pg_plan_advice and any future affected module.
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund posted the generic fix, and Maksim Melnikov and Zsolt Parragi agreed with it; Maksim added it to the CommitFest as v3. Nobody has decided on backpatching, and Maksim's idea of moving the rule into src/Makefile.global.in got no reply.
unclear: The thread does not say how the change could break extensions, or which extension setups would be at risk.
The v3 commit message says only MODULES; the thread does not say whether PROGRAM or MODULE_big targets in pgxs need the same rule.
The thread does not say whether the meson build has the same race.
Nobody answered whether the per-module v2 fix should go to back branches.
search_queries: bc file depends on o file

objections.title: Stated scope covers MODULES only, not MODULE_big or PROGRAM objects
objections.failure_scenario: An out-of-tree extension builds with MODULE_big and a bison-generated header under --with-llvm and make -j. Its .bc files carry no dependency on the .o files, so the build fails at random. The author finds out from a packager's failed build.
objections.argument: The v3 commit message says the .bc files "for MODULES" now depend on their .o files. pgxs also builds bitcode for OBJS under MODULE_big, and the thread does not say whether those targets get the same rule. Message #4 counts on the fix to cover pg_plan_advice "and all future cases", which holds only if every bitcode path in pgxs.mk gets the dependency. If one path is left out, the next module with a generated header hits the same race, and nothing in the build warns about the gap.
objections.author_must_show: Does v3 add the .bc-on-.o dependency for every bitcode target pgxs.mk builds, including MODULE_big OBJS, and is pg_plan_advice fixed by it?

critic.reasoning: contrib/cube and contrib/seg build with MODULE_big and OBJS, so a fix for the reported failure has to cover that path. But the v3 commit message names only MODULES, and no message confirms a test of v3, so the question stands.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes dependency rules in src/makefiles/pgxs.mk, which out-of-tree extensions use to build bitcode.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: Message #2 leans toward master only for fear of breaking extensions; nobody answered the per-module backpatch idea in message #3.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The .bc-on-.o rule would exist in both common.mk and pgxs.mk, and each bitcode path in pgxs.mk needs it.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does v3 add the .bc-on-.o dependency for every bitcode target pgxs.mk builds, including MODULE_big OBJS, which contrib/cube and contrib/seg use?
Has anyone run `make -C contrib/cube cubescan.bc` and a parallel build of pg_plan_advice with v3 applied, and did both succeed?
Which extension setup could break if the pgxs.mk change were backpatched, as message #2 fears?
Should back branches get the per-module v2 fix for cube and seg, or no fix at all?
Does the meson build have the same race between bitcode compilation and bison-generated headers?

committability.owner_note: Andres Freund wrote the generic fix in message #2 and says he wrote the original backend rule; the owner needs to know the make build system and LLVM bitcode rules.
committability.liability: The owner signs for build behaviour of every pgxs extension built with --with-llvm, including out-of-tree ones, for as long as the make build is supported.
committability.author_follow_up: Maksim Melnikov replied within three days and registered v3 in the CommitFest; no sign either way from Andres Freund after message #2 in the visible thread.

priority.reason: The patch is about 2 KiB, touches two makefiles, and fixes a build failure reported for cube, seg and pg_plan_advice. It copies an existing rule, so the project carries little new after commit.

provisional_note: Without the code, it cannot be confirmed which pgxs.mk bitcode targets get the new dependency, or what the change to src/backend/common.mk does. The commit message names only MODULES.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add llvm version into the version string
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the LLVM version to PG_VERSION_STR, the way the gcc version is already shown, so that JIT bug reports include it. A later version takes the runtime version from the loaded library through LLVMGetVersion, an API that exists from LLVM 16 on.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the configure-time llvm-config version may not match the library loaded at run time. He also objected that changing what version() returns can break code that parses it, and that adding subsystem versions to it does not scale to ICU or libxml2. He suggested a new system view instead, the author agreed to try that direction, and others proposed showing both build-time and runtime versions in the view.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Adding rows to a view over time seems way less likely to cause
problems than messing with a string people probably have crufty
parsing code for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix race condition in SSI when reading PredXact->SxactGlobalXmin
precedents_retrieved.summary: DropAllPredicateLocksFromTable, PredicateLockPageSplit and CheckTableForSerializableConflictIn read PredXact->SxactGlobalXmin without a lock and can see InvalidTransactionId while SetNewSxactGlobalXmin recomputes it, then skip needed SIRead lock work. The attached patch takes SerializableXactHashLock for these reads; the author also described an alternative where SetNewSxactGlobalXmin assigns the new xmin only after the scan.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one objected to the fix. The entry was withdrawn the day the author pointed out that two commitfest entries existed for the same patch (6037, his own, and 6145, registered by Mihail Nikalayeu), so it was probably closed as a duplicate. The visible messages do not say which entry was withdrawn. A .spec reproducer with injection points was requested and still pending.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I guess one of the commitfest entries should be deleted? I had already made
one already.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid orphaned dependencies
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch prevents orphaned pg_depend and pg_shdepend entries by using a new dirty catalog snapshot whenever a dependency is recorded. It checks for in-flight transactions that affect the referenced object and raises an error if it finds one, without using locks.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the global variable that switches catalog lookups to a dirty snapshot is unsafe, since a syscache entry could be built from a row that may never commit. He also showed that the patch does not close the race: if DROP scans for dependents before CREATE adds and commits its entry, the orphan still appears. He suggested that creation DDL instead lock each referenced object in recordDependency. The entry then waited on the author until it was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE"".
Reverted commit(s): Avoid race condition between "GRANT role" and "DROP ROLE".
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 98fc31d6499163a0a781aa6f13582a07f09cd7c6.
That change allowed DROP OWNED BY to drop grants of the target
role to other roles, arguing that nobody would need those
privileges anymore.  But that's not so: if you're not superuser,
you still need admin privilege on the target role so you can
drop it.

It's not clear whether or how the dependency-based approach
to solving the original problem can be adapted to keep these
grants.  Since v18 release is fast approaching, the sanest
thing to do seems to be to revert this patch for now.  The
race-condition problem is low severity and not worth taking
risks for.

I didn't force a catversion bump in 98fc31d64, so I won't do
so here either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow COPY "text" to output a header and add header matching mode to COPY FROM
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets COPY write and read a HEADER line in the text format, which before was allowed only in CSV mode. A later version also adds HEADER match to COPY FROM, which requires the header line to match the target column names in both text and CSV format.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback after the v5 revision. He judged it wrong to treat HEADER as a boolean-like option with one extra "match" value, and suggested a separate option for clear semantics. He also asked that repeated HEADER options be detected as redundant, as COPY does for "format". The first 2018 version was returned earlier because his review, which also raised header matching, was not addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It seems to me that we may
actually be looking at having this stuff as an option different than
"header" at the end to have clear semantics.

precedents_retrieved.title: Close race in DROP TABLESPACE on Windows
precedents_retrieved.summary: On Windows, DROP TABLESPACE can fail with "tablespace is not empty" because another backend still holds an open descriptor on an unlinked file, which Windows keeps in the directory. Noah Misch proposed that DROP TABLESPACE wait for other backends to close such files, for example by polling with a new wait_unlinked_files() function.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No code was written. Noah Misch recorded the fix as a TODO and changed the regression test to use RESET ROLE instead of \c -, so only one backend is involved. Amit Kapila said the wait could last until the other backend runs another command. Alternatives (a catchup interrupt, renaming files to the tablespace top-level directory before unlink) were left for whoever decides to work on the issue.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think we can discuss further about which approach is better, once someone decides to work on this issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: create index failed. PARALLEL UNSAFE function does not prevent parallel index build
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch made plan_create_index_workers() check parallel safety on the raw index expressions and predicate, read from the pg_index syscache, so that a PARALLEL UNSAFE function folded to a constant still prevents a parallel index build. The bug report showed CREATE INDEX failing in a parallel worker because a plpgsql function with an EXCEPTION block was const-folded before the check.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was committed and then reverted after Tom Lane objected. He said it does not fix the failure, which returns when the function is marked PARALLEL SAFE, and that it breaks the planner rule that original markings stop mattering once a function is inlined or const-folded. He also said that passing raw parse-analysis output to is_parallel_safe() misses parallel-unsafe default arguments, and he preferred making exception-using functions parallel safe through a separate commitfest patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's a band-aid
that doesn't really solve the problem: if I simply declare the
function as PARALLEL SAFE, the failure comes right back.

precedents_retrieved.title: Enable jitlink as an alternative jit linker of legacy Rtdyld and add riscv jitting support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets the LLVM JIT provider use JITLink (ObjectLinkingLayer) in place of RuntimeDyld, through a new C++ wrapper because LLVM has no C API for it. It turns this on for riscv with LLVM 15 or later and hard-codes riscv ABI names, CPU features, PIC relocation and the medium code model.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund said the riscv ABI and target machine settings belong in LLVM, and that the missing JITLink C API should be proposed to LLVM. Thomas Munro asked why JITLink was used only for riscv and why riscv needed manual feature and ABI selection. The author agreed to try the LLVM patches later and asked to keep the workarounds meanwhile. No reviewer replied after that, and no new patch version appears.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think this is something that should go into the llvm code, rather than
postgres.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 45b7abe59e9485657ac9380f35d2d917dd0da25b.

It turns out that the %name-prefix syntax without "=" does not work
at all in pre-2.4 Bison.  We are not prepared to make such a large
jump in minimum required Bison version just to suppress a warning
message in a version hardly any developers are using yet.
When 3.0 gets more popular, we'll figure out a way to deal with this.
In the meantime, BISONFLAGS=-Wno-deprecated is recommendable for
anyone using 3.0 who doesn't want to see the warning.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P9] reverted a dtrace makefile dependency change because it broke parallel builds, but it only shares the area. This patch adds an ordering edge from each .bc file to its .o file, and src/backend/common.mk already uses that pattern, so the [P9] reason does not carry over. The thread cites no earlier attempt at this fix.

The change brings pgxs.mk in line with the rule src/backend/common.mk already uses, and adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object or dump state. Message #2 names a backpatch risk for extensions but gives no concrete setup that breaks, and the proposal targets master only, so no failure scenario can be written. Open points that need the code: whether MODULE_big OBJS bitcode gets the same rule, and whether meson has the same race. [P9] is about dtrace dependencies and does not apply here.

The proposal changes only make dependency rules in pgxs.mk and src/backend/common.mk. It touches no on-disk format, WAL, catalog, replication, wire protocol or C ABI, so this angle has nothing to object to; the pgxs effect on out-of-tree extension builds belongs to another angle.

The change only adds make dependencies so that .bc files wait for their .o files in pgxs builds. It touches no privilege checks, roles, data access paths, authentication, or server runtime behaviour, so it has no security or privilege aspect to object to.

The core idea fits core well. It copies the rule src/backend/common.mk already uses, adds no hot-path cost, and a committer who knows this area wrote it. The one objection is about scope, and a new version can fix it.

This is a build-system bug fix. Nothing in Postgres or in an extension already makes .bc files for pgxs MODULES wait for generated headers. The patch copies the existing rule in src/backend/common.mk instead of adding a second mechanism, so the existing-feature and extension angle has nothing to raise. [P9] is about dtrace dependencies and does not apply.

Demand is shown. This is a build bug that fails `make world-bin -j3` with --with-llvm, and two people reported it independently for cube and seg (message #1) and for pg_plan_advice (message #4). The fix mirrors existing practice in src/backend/common.mk, and the cost falls only on LLVM builds of pgxs modules.
